messages.subject: Replications not convergent
parts:
Hello everyone, 
for my Bachelor thesis, I have to conduct a power analysis for a moderated mediation model in which X is continous, W Categorical, and all endogenous variables are continuous
I am interested in the moderation of the a-path (hayes model 7).
I followed the tutorial "Single and Multigroup Moderated Mediation Models" in Donnelly et al. 2021, and adapted the code according to my research question. That is X ranges from 1-5, according to scoring on the questionnaire is use. Also, I used the simsem::find() function to find appropriate residual variances, as suggested here: https://groups.google.com/g/lavaan/c/UUjO8H7Pvzg

I increased nrep stepwise, however the replications do not converge. What can I do? 
(screenshot of code is in appended)

Thank you for your help!

parts:
Hi Andi,

I don't have a solution, but I have a couple of suggestions. 

 - Paste your code into the email - that way if someone wants to try it to run it, they can.

 - Include all your code - you (presumably) have some library calls at the top, but I don't know what they are. You have a function called model.path(), but I don't know where this comes from (and sometimes this can be worse, I can assume I know the package it comes from, but it actually comes from a different package.

- I'm not familiar with the paper Donnelly et al. 2021. If you post the full reference, I can find it. Even better, save me the effort and give me a link to click on. Even more better, if you can, make sure that the link is not behind a paywall. You might have access, but I might not. 

- Bonus suggestion: you can avoid the problem above by qualifying your function names - that is specifying the package the function comes from, by writing: package::function(). That makes it easier to read and can also avoid some problems. Example:
Let's say you're running your model, so you load the lavaan package and run your model:

  library(lavaan)
  sem(my_model, my_data)

You want to explore a bit, so you load the sem package:

   library(sem)

Now you run:

  sem(my_model, my_data)

And you get all sorts of weird errors (or perhaps worse, you don't get all sorts of weird errors).  The first time you ran the sem command, it used lavaan::sem(), the second time it used sem::sem(), so the running the same code in the same file did a different thing - this can be very irritating to debug (and it might be that you didn't even load the sem package, but you loaded another package that had sem as a dependency.  You might have even done this in a separate R script that you were doing something different in. (So you restart R and the error disappears.)

Avoid this by running:

sem::sem(my_model, my_data)

Or 

lavaan::sem(my_model, my_data)

Apologies that that email got quite long, and also didn't answer your question. If I didn't have some work to do, I wouldn't have spent the time on this. :) 

Good luck!

jeremy

parts:
thank you for the suggestions! the simsem package is used, and i adapted the code from here: https://link.springer.com/article/10.3758/s13428-022-01996-0
the model syntax: userParams <- "..." is specified with lavaan package syntax 

N.per.group <- 50 # balanced group sample sizes
designMatrix <- expand.grid(X = 1, W = 1:0)
designMatrix$XW <- designMatrix$X * designMatrix$W # interaction
exoData <- do.call(rbind, lapply(1:N.per.group, function(i)
  designMatrix))
exoData$X <- sample(1:5, size = 100, replace = TRUE)

a.w0 <- .5 # effect of X on M when moderator (W) == 0
a.mod <- .3 # how much “a” path is moderated by W (i.e., interaction)
b.w0 <- .4 # effect of M on Y when moderator (W) == 0
b.mod <- 0 # no moderating effect on “b” path
c.w0 <-.2 # effect of X on Y when moderator (W) == 0
c.mod <- 0 # no moderating effect on “c” path
w.M <- .2 # simple effect of moderator (W) on M when X == 0
w.Y <- -.1 # simple effect of moderator (W) on Y when X == 0
kappa.free <- kappa.pop <- matrix(NA, # estimate all effects
                                     nrow = 2, # 2 outcomes (M and Y)
                                     ncol = 3, # dummy coded X, W, XW
                                     dimnames = list(c("M", "Y"),names(exoData)))
kappa.free["M","X"] <- "a.w0" # label free parameters
kappa.free["M","W"] <- "w.M" # (to define indirect effects)
kappa.free["M","XW"] <- "a.mod"
kappa.free["Y","X"] <- "c.w0"
kappa.free["Y","W"] <- "w.Y"
kappa.free["Y","XW"] <- 0 # fixed to 0; label “c.mod” to free
kappa.pop["M","X"] <- a.w0 # set population parameters
kappa.pop["M","W"] <- w.M # (defined above)
kappa.pop["M","XW"] <- a.mod
kappa.pop["Y","X"] <- c.w0
kappa.pop["Y","W"] <- w.Y
kappa.pop["Y","XW"] <- c.mod
exoPaths <- bind(free = kappa.free, popParam = kappa.pop)
beta.free <- beta.pop <- matrix(0, nrow = 2, ncol = 2,
                                   dimnames = list(c("M","Y"), c("M","Y")))
beta.free["Y","M"] <- "b"
beta.pop["Y","M"] <- b.w0
endoPaths <- bind(free = beta.free, popParam = beta.pop)
(exoCov <- cov.wt(exoData, method = "ML"))$cov
residVar <- findFactorResidualVar(beta = beta.pop, corPsi = diag(2),
                                  gamma = kappa.pop, covcov = exoCov$cov)
(heteroVar <- list(binds(free = diag(as.numeric(NA), 2),
                         popParam = residVar)))
userParams <- '
ind.w0 := a.w0 * b
ind.w1 := (a.w0 + a.mod) * b
ind.diff := a.mod * b

'

modMed1 <- simsem::model.path(BE = endoPaths, RPS = residCor,
                         KA = exoPaths, con = userParams,
                         indLab = rownames(kappa.free),
                         covLab = colnames(kappa.free))
sim1 <- sim(nRep = 10, model = modMed1, covData = exoData,
               n = nrow(exoData), seed = 2023, outfun = rejectMCCI,
               meanstructure = FALSE)
rejectMCCI <- function(object){
  CIs <- semTools::monteCarloCI(object)
  apply(CIs, margin = 1, function(CI) 0 < CI["ci.lower"] | 0 > CI["ci.upper"])
}


summaryParam(sim1, matchParam = TRUE, digits = 3)
testMCCI <- do.call(rbind, simsem::getExtraOutput(sim1))
colMeans(testMCCI) # empirical estimate of power for Monte Carlo CIs

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Replications not convergent
parts:
The design matrix calculates the interaction XW prior to setting X's actual (Likert-scale?) values of 1-5. So XW simply = W, which expect would not allow your model to converge because the sample covariance matrix would not be positive definite if 2 predictors are perfectly correlated.

Since you have a Likert-scale predictor, I would recommend you think more carefully about the response distribution you expect (which seems random, not fixed, invalidating the exogeneity assumption of your simulation.)  If you really think that the distribution of X is fixed (i.e., has specific probabilities for each response option), you should first generate a sample of minimal size with that property.  For example, assuming something normalish looking:

(X <- rep(1:5, times = c(.1, .2, .4, .2, .1)*10))
W <- 1:0
expand.grid(X, W)

That leads to orthogonal X and W, then you create their interaction term XW.  That basic building block (here, 20 observations) can be repeated however often to yield samples of different sizes following that fixed design (e.g., 5 of those yield N = 100).

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

Thanks, but this is not a reprex.  There is no object "heteroVar" when trying to make the object modMed1.  Try clearing your workspace before running the reprex yourself.

rm(list = ls())

Also, did you notice your residual variance is negative:

> (diag(residVar))
        [,1] [,2]
[1,] -0.1925    0
[2,]  0.0000  NaN

That means your population slopes cannot be interpreted as standardized slopes (their model-implied explained variance exceeds 1).

parts:
Thank you for the reprex.  As I pointed out before, your mediator's residual variance is negative, so your effects are too big to be interpreted in units of SD, i.e., your explained variance is > 1. 

If I simply lower your moderator's effect to a.mod <- .2,  the simulation works fine, after also changing some typos.  Bear in mind that R is case-sensitive:
  • In the sim() function, the argument is nRep= not nrep= 
  • In your rejectMCCI() function definition, the apply() function's second argument is MARGIN= not margin= 
5000 reps is not necessary to demonstrate the issue, so I just run 5 reps in the reprex below:

library(simsem)

rejectMCCI <- function(object) {
  CIs <- semTools::monteCarloCI(object)
apply(CIs, MARGIN = 1, function(CI) 0 < CI["ci.lower"] | 0 > CI["ci.upper"] )

}


N.per.group <- 50 # balanced group sample sizes

X <- rep(1:5, size = c(.1, .2, .4, .2, .1)*10)
W <- 1:0
designMatrix <- expand.grid(X = X, W = W)
designMatrix$XW <- designMatrix$X * designMatrix$W # interaction
exoData <- do.call(rbind, lapply(1:N.per.group, function(i) designMatrix))

a.w0 <- .5 # effect of X on M when moderator (W) == 0
a.mod <- .2 # how much “a” path is moderated by W (i.e., interaction)

b.w0 <- .4 # effect of M on Y when moderator (W) == 0
b.mod <- 0 # no moderating effect on “b” path
c.w0 <-.2 # effect of X on Y when moderator (W) == 0
c.mod <- 0 # no moderating effect on “c” path
w.M <- .2 # simple effect of moderator (W) on M when X == 0
w.Y <- .2 # simple effect of moderator (W) on Y when X == 0
kappa.free <- kappa.pop <- matrix(NA, # estimate all effects
                                  nrow = 2, # 2 outcomes (M and Y)
                                  ncol = 3, # dummy coded X, W, XW
                                  dimnames = list(c("M", "Y"),names(exoData)))
kappa.free["M","X"] <- "a.w0" # label free parameters
kappa.free["M","W"] <- 0 # (to define indirect effects)
kappa.free["M","XW"] <- "a.mod"
kappa.free["Y","X"] <- "c.w0"
kappa.free["Y","W"] <- 0
kappa.free["Y","XW"] <- 0 # fixed to 0; label “c.mod” to free
kappa.pop["M","X"] <- a.w0 # set population parameters
kappa.pop["M","W"] <- w.M # (defined above)
kappa.pop["M","XW"] <- a.mod
kappa.pop["Y","X"] <- c.w0
kappa.pop["Y","W"] <- w.Y
kappa.pop["Y","XW"] <- c.mod
exoPaths <- bind(free = kappa.free, popParam = kappa.pop)
beta.free <- beta.pop <- matrix(0, nrow = 2, ncol = 2,
                                dimnames = list(c("M","Y"), c("M","Y")))
beta.free["Y","M"] <- "b"
beta.pop["Y","M"] <- b.w0
endoPaths <- bind(free = beta.free, popParam = beta.pop)
exoCov <- cov.wt(exoData, method = "ML")$cov
residVar <- findFactorResidualVar(beta = beta.pop, corPsi = diag(2),
                                  gamma = kappa.pop, covcov = exoCov)


(diag(residVar))
resEq <- binds(free = diag(as.numeric(NA), 2), popParam = diag(residVar))

userParams <- '
ind.w0 := a.w0 * b
ind.w1 := (a.w0 + a.mod) * b
ind.diff := a.mod * b
'

modMed1 <- model.path(BE = endoPaths,  PS = resEq,
                      KA = exoPaths, con = userParams,
                      indLab = rownames(kappa.free),
                      covLab = colnames(kappa.free))
sim1 <- sim(nRep = 5, model = modMed1, covData = exoData, n = nrow(exoData), seed = 1027,
outfun = rejectMCCI, meanstructure = FALSE)
summaryParam(sim1, matchParam = TRUE, digits = 3, detail = T)

testMCCI <- do.call(rbind, getExtraOutput(sim1))
colMeans(testMCCI)

While working on this example, I found a bug that mistakenly transformed what getExtraOutput() should return.  So you can install the latest development version (0.5-16.911) again before running it with many replications.
